content.text:
**Currently, the app can fund one more user using all five reports.** The immediate bottleneck is Hunchlane’s internal budget.

Live snapshot checked October 12:

| Limit | Usage / remaining | Capacity at 5 reports per user |
|---|---|---|
| **App budget** | $7.20 reserved of $15; **$7.80 remaining** | **1 additional user**, with 2 reports left over |
| **Crustdata** | **5,175 credits available**; app allowance has **4,965 unallocated** | **198 additional users**, considering Crustdata alone |
| **Sponsored Claude/LiteLLM API** | $0.5205 spent of $20; **$19.4795 remaining**; 60 requests/minute | Depends on actual tokens per report |
| **Neatlogs** | Account quota unavailable; dashboard requires sign-in | Unverified |
| **Inngest** | Local configuration uses development mode; Cloud usage unavailable | Unverified |

The app reserves **$0.75 per full report plus $0.30 per new intake conversation**. Assuming each report starts a new conversation:

**$7.80 ÷ $1.05 = 7 more reports → 1 user’s full five-report allowance.**

Without new intake conversations, it can admit **10 reports → 2 users**. These are reservations, not actual provider charges; failures keep their reservations. See [budget constants](/Users/nikhil/Developer/hunchlane/src/core/budget.ts:1).

A full report normally uses:

- **3 model calls**, plus up to **3 intake calls**.
- **2 Crustdata searches + 1 batched fetch**, costing up to **5 credits**.
- Approximately **20–23 Inngest executions**, before retries.

**Inngest has a potential quota drain:** the registered recovery job runs every minute. With its three baseline steps, that is roughly **172,800 executions per 30 days**, even without report work, if deployed to Cloud with the schema ready. Inngest Free includes **50,000 executions/month**, so this job alone could exhaust it in about **8.7 days**. [Recovery job](/Users/nikhil/Developer/hunchlane/src/server/inngest.ts:78) · [Inngest pricing](https://www.inngest.com/pricing)

Also, the code allows **five refinements alongside five full reports**. Fully using both, with five intake conversations, reserves **$7.25 and 50 Crustdata credits per user**.

**Planning number: one additional fully consuming user under today’s app cap.** The 198-user Crustdata figure is only a provider-specific ceiling; it isn’t overall capacity until model costs, Neatlogs quota, and Cloud Inngest usage are verified. No limits were changed or paid research calls made.
what is app budget ?

The **app budget is a spending guardrail built into Hunchlane**, stored in your database. It’s separate from your provider balances.

It’s currently set to **$15**. Before starting work, the app reserves:

- **$0.75** per full report
- **$0.30** per new intake conversation
- **$0.40** per refinement

So far, **$7.20 has been reserved**, leaving **$7.80**. Reserved money isn’t necessarily money actually spent—the app conservatively keeps reservations even after failures.

When that $15 allowance fills up, Hunchlane blocks new work **even if Crustdata and Claude still have credits**. That’s why the current capacity looks so low.
why do we have that ?

It was added as a **hackathon safety cap** to prevent unexpected API spending if many people started reports or requests failed.

But it’s conservative: it reserves fixed amounts and doesn’t release unused reservations. Sponsored Claude calls also count toward it even though they use your separate $20 sponsor allowance.

So it’s now restricting access much sooner than your provider balances require. **The protection is useful, but the $15 cap and accounting need adjusting to match your actual allowances.**
if we remove the app budget.. what will exhaust first and what will happen ?

**If we remove only the app’s dollar cap, Inngest is the likely first bottleneck on Cloud.** If you’re running Inngest locally, the sponsored Claude budget is likely next—but we haven’t measured enough report costs to confirm.

| Limit reached | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Inngest Cloud Free** | Background execution pauses. Reports may remain queued or unfinished until the quota resets or you upgrade. |
| **Claude/LiteLLM’s $20 budget** | Model requests are rejected. Intake or research fails; the app cannot finish the report. |
| **Crustdata allowance** | The separate credit reservation gate blocks new research. If the provider balance is exhausted first, its preflight blocks research. |
| **Neatlogs quota** | Impact is unverified; telemetry initialization is on the report execution path, so we shouldn’t assume only logging is affected. |

The biggest known issue is the **every-minute Inngest recovery job**. On Cloud Free, its baseline workload could consume the entire 50,000-execution quota in about **8.7 days**, even without users. [Inngest limits](https://www.inngest.com/pricing)

Crustdata has enough unallocated app allowance for **198 more users × five full reports**. Claude has **$19.48 remaining**, but its user capacity depends on input and output tokens.

**Removing the cap alone won’t give us a reliable capacity number.** We should first fix the recovery job’s idle usage and measure the model cost of completed reports. Also, the current dollar reservation code would need changing—simply deleting the budget row would block all new work.

content.text:
The current integration is incomplete: it requires financial inputs in the brief, a verified CFO.ai recipe, and a parser for CFO.ai’s actual results. The Numbers tab currently starts with generic local assumptions rather than the report’s saved inputs.

CFO.ai can create saved models and scenarios through MCP, but we need to inspect its authenticated tool schema before implementing the adapter. [CFO.ai MCP documentation](https://docs.cfo.ai/integrations/mcp-server)

The key product choice is where each report’s financial assumptions should come from.

questions.question: How should a new report get its financial assumptions?

options.label: Suggested starting model (Recommended)
options.description: Generate clearly labeled estimates from the idea and research, cite any sourced values, and let users adjust them afterward.

options.label: User inputs first
options.description: Ask users for price, costs, and sales assumptions before creating a CFO.ai model.

options.label: Optional after report
options.description: Finish research first, then offer a separate action in Numbers to supply inputs and create a model.

questions.question: What should the first version of Numbers show?

options.label: Simple viability model (Recommended)
options.description: Price, unit costs, fixed costs, monthly sales, break-even, and three 12-month scenarios.

options.label: Detailed business model
options.description: Add acquisition costs, churn or repeat purchases, staffing, startup costs, and runway using business-specific models.

questions.question: Which CFO.ai account setup should power reports?

options.label: Hunchlane workspace (Recommended)
options.description: One app-managed connection with isolated models per report; users see results inside Hunchlane.

options.label: Each user's account
options.description: Users connect their own CFO.ai workspace before modeling, with more onboarding and credential management.

content.text:
That gives us a clear direction: Hunchlane suggests a starting model, CFO.ai calculates and saves three scenarios, and users explore the results in Numbers. Each input should show whether it came from the user, a cited source, or an estimate.

Local configuration has none of the CFO.ai setup enabled yet, so connecting the dedicated workspace and verifying its results will be the first implementation milestone. I’d keep report reading and slider changes free of new provider calls, and keep shared-workspace CFO.ai links out of public reports.

questions.question: How should we choose the model's currency when the user hasn't specified one?

options.label: Location, then USD (Recommended)
options.description: Use INR for India, EUR or GBP for explicit matching locations, and USD otherwise; label the choice as an assumption.

options.label: Always INR
options.description: Use INR for every suggested model unless the user changes it.

options.label: Always USD
options.description: Use USD for every suggested model unless the user changes it.

questions.question: What should happen when a user changes the suggested numbers?

options.label: Local what-if only (Recommended)
options.description: Update calculations instantly in the browser; keep the original saved CFO.ai model unchanged.

options.label: Save revised CFO model
options.description: Add an explicit save action that creates a versioned CFO.ai model with additional provider work.

questions.question: Should this release create financial models for existing reports?

options.label: New reports only (Recommended)
options.description: Model new reports automatically; existing reports retain their local explorer without automatic spending.

options.label: On-demand for old reports
options.description: Also offer existing report owners a one-time Create model action.

questions.question: Should research appear immediately while the financial model finishes?

options.label: Show report, then numbers (Recommended)
options.description: Save the research report first; Numbers shows a preparing state and updates when CFO.ai readback is verified.

options.label: Finish together
options.description: Keep the report in progress until the model finishes or reaches its time limit.

questions.question: If CFO.ai is unavailable, what should the Numbers tab show?

options.label: Labeled local model (Recommended)
options.description: Use the suggested assumptions for local calculations and clearly state that CFO.ai did not produce a verified model.

options.label: No suggested results
options.description: Show the failure and let the user enter their own assumptions in the local explorer.

<proposed_plan>
# CFO.ai models for the Numbers tab

## Summary

For new reports, Hunchlane will suggest financial assumptions in **USD**, create an isolated model in the dedicated CFO.ai workspace, and display verified results in Numbers.

Research appears first; financial modeling runs afterward. User adjustments calculate local what-if scenarios without further CFO.ai calls.

## Model and presentation

- Use the existing simple model: price, variable cost per sale/customer, monthly fixed costs, starting monthly sales/customers, monthly growth, and optional starting cash.
- Label each input as **User supplied**, **Suggested estimate**, or **Sourced benchmark**, with its explanation and validated citations. Competitor pricing remains a benchmark; the proposed product’s price remains an assumption. Do not convert foreign-currency benchmarks without a verified exchange rate.
- Leave starting cash unknown unless supplied. Clearly describe sales and growth as assumptions, not evidence of demand.
- Retain the existing Conservative/Base/Optimistic calculations and 12-month horizon. Show revenue, operating profit, contribution margin, monthly break-even, and cash only when starting cash is known.
- Initialize the explorer from the saved model. Changing inputs updates local calculations; **Reset to saved model** restores the original assumptions. Exports include the saved model, excluding unsaved adjustments.
- While pending, display **“Preparing your numbers…”**. When no verified model is available, show a blurred decorative placeholder with **“Numbers coming soon.”** Keep placeholder figures out of the DOM and accessibility tree. Do not expose errors, technical status, or fabricated results.

## Integration and durable execution

- First configure the operator’s encrypted OAuth connection and dedicated workspace. Inspect the authenticated MCP schema and model-building instructions; implement a typed adapter and native-result parser from actual receipts, replacing the unverified generic recipe contract.
- Use reviewed formula templates with validated numeric inputs. Namespace every page, table, and variable by report ID. Never let research text select tools, workspace references, or formulas. Keep shared-workspace URLs and raw provider receipts server-only.
- Create one financial job per newly admitted report, reserving an additional **25 cents for assumption generation**. Verify CFO.ai’s actual metering and persist its required allowance before enabling model writes; do not assume those calls are free.
- Save the research report and financial dispatch intent atomically. A separate Inngest worker generates assumptions, creates the CFO.ai model, reads its calculated values, and checks them independently against the domain calculations.
- Journal each provider operation separately. Persist returned references before advancing. An uncertain write stops for read-only reconciliation; never repeat creation blindly. Serialize OAuth refresh and CFO.ai model writes.
- Give financial jobs a ten-minute deadline. CFO.ai failure must leave the research report intact and transition Numbers to the quiet “coming soon” state. Reuse the existing recovery dispatcher for financial outbox delivery rather than adding another frequent cron.

## Interfaces and compatibility

- Add a versioned financial payload containing presentation state (`pending`, `verified`, `unavailable`), assumptions with provenance, currency, scenarios, and completion time. Normalize existing financial payloads for compatibility.
- Add a persisted financial-job record with owner, report ID, reservation, cursor, deadline, lease, and dispatch state. Enforce one job per report.
- Return updated financial data through the existing owner-checked report API. Continue polling every three seconds while finance is pending and the report is visible; stop on completion, deadline, or navigation.
- Update only the report’s financial section after verification. Keep research content and existing public-share snapshots immutable. Shares created while finance is pending show “Numbers coming soon” permanently for that snapshot.
- Existing reports receive no automatic models or backfill. Disable new financial jobs until authenticated create/readback and isolation checks pass.

## Validation and rollout

- Test provenance and citation validation, USD defaults, missing capital, zero sales, negative contribution, and all three business categories.
- Verify monthly values, month ordering, scenario uniqueness, annual totals, and break-even against CFO.ai readback. Test partial responses, arithmetic mismatches, uncertain writes, token refresh, duplicate dispatch, and worker restarts.
- Verify owner isolation, preservation of existing reports and shares, and that reading reports or adjusting inputs causes no paid calls.
- Render desktop/mobile pending, verified, and coming-soon states; exercise keyboard controls, local edits/reset, reduced motion, and Markdown exports.
- Run `pnpm check`, relevant `pnpm test:browser` checks, and `pnpm build`. Enable only after two independent report models demonstrate isolation and verified results; monitor job completion, reconciliation counts, latency, and provider usage without logging private inputs.
</proposed_plan>

- **Consider CFO.ai later as an explicit “Build a financial model” action** for users who need it.

That keeps basic research fast and gives CFO.ai a focused purpose.
